q: What is fine-tuning and when would you use it?
short: Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a smaller, targeted dataset to change its behaviour: follow instructions, adopt a format or style, specialise in a task or domain. Use it when prompting isn't enough and you have good examples; use retrieval for fresh facts.
mistakes: Fine-tuning to inject frequently changing facts.

q: What is SFT?
short: Supervised fine-tuning on (prompt, ideal response) pairs with next-token cross-entropy, typically masking prompt tokens so only the response is learned.
mistakes: Including prompt tokens in the loss by accident.

q: What is instruction tuning?
short: SFT over a large mixture of tasks expressed as natural-language instructions, which teaches the model to follow instructions in general, improving zero-shot performance on unseen tasks.

q: What is LoRA?
short: Low-Rank Adaptation: freeze W and learn ΔW = BA with small rank r, training r(d + k) parameters per matrix; B starts at zero and BA can be merged into W after training.
mistakes: Thinking LoRA adds inference latency after merging.

q: What is QLoRA?
short: LoRA training where the frozen base model is stored in 4-bit (NF4 with double quantization) and paged optimizers handle memory spikes, enabling fine-tuning of large models on a single GPU with near-16-bit quality.

q: Prompt tuning vs prefix tuning?
short: Prompt tuning learns embeddings for n virtual tokens at the input only; prefix tuning learns key/value vectors prepended at every layer, giving more capacity (n·L·2d vs n·d).

q: What is catastrophic forgetting?
short: When fine-tuning on new data overwrites weights supporting earlier abilities, degrading general knowledge or other skills.
detail: Narrow data, high LR, many epochs worsen it.

q: What is knowledge distillation?
short: Training a smaller student to imitate a larger teacher, using the teacher's softened probabilities (temperature T) and/or teacher-generated outputs as targets.
mistakes: Using only hard labels and expecting the same gain.

q: LoRA r = 16 on Q and V (4096 × 4096) in 32 layers: trainable parameters?
short: Per matrix 16 × 8192 = 131,072; × 2 matrices × 32 layers ≈ 8.4M (0.12% of 7B).
detail: Add MLP projections to grow it.

q: Why does LoRA work?
short: Adaptation updates appear to have low intrinsic rank: the model already has the needed features, and the task mostly re-weights a small subspace, which a rank-r product can express.
mistakes: Claiming LoRA equals full fine-tuning always.

q: LoRA vs adapters?
short: LoRA adds a parallel low-rank update that can be merged into W (no latency); adapters insert sequential bottleneck layers that remain at inference (small latency) but are modular.
mistakes: Calling LoRA an adapter layer inserted in sequence.

q: How does model merging with task vectors work?
short: Compute τᵢ = θᵢ − θ_base for each fine-tuned model sharing a base, then add (scaled) task vectors to the base; trim small or conflicting entries (TIES, DARE) to reduce interference.

q: Why multiply the distillation KL by T²?
short: Gradients of the softened KL scale as 1/T², so multiplying by T² keeps their magnitude comparable to the hard-label loss as T changes.

q: Plan SFT for a customer-support assistant.
short: Collect real tickets and expert replies, de-identify, write guidelines, build a few thousand diverse examples in the production chat template, mask prompts, fine-tune with LoRA, hold out a test set, evaluate helpfulness, accuracy, tone and safety, then iterate.
follow: How to handle facts that change?

q: How do you reduce catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning?
short: Mix general instruction data with task data (replay), use PEFT, small LR and few epochs, regularise toward the base (KL or weight penalties), and evaluate on broad benchmarks and safety suites.

q: Fine-tune a 70B model on one 80 GB GPU: how?
short: QLoRA: 4-bit NF4 base (~35 GB), LoRA on attention and MLP projections, gradient checkpointing, paged optimizers, small micro-batch with gradient accumulation, FlashAttention, bf16 compute.

q: Can fine-tuning reliably add new factual knowledge?
short: Not reliably: models absorb new facts slowly, may hallucinate more when trained on unfamiliar facts, and knowledge goes stale; retrieval augmentation is preferred for facts, fine-tuning for behaviour and format.
detail: Continued pre-training helps for whole domains.

q: Distillation via logits vs via generated data?
short: Logit distillation matches the teacher's full distribution per token (rich signal, needs teacher logits and same tokenizer); data distillation fine-tunes on teacher-generated responses or reasoning traces (works across tokenizers and APIs, less signal per token).
mistakes: Assuming the same tokenizer isn't needed for logits.

q: Why might benign fine-tuning weaken safety behaviour?
short: Refusal and safety behaviours live in weights shared with general skills; small updates toward a narrow distribution can shift them, especially without safety data in the mix, so safety must be re-evaluated and refreshed.

q: Serve 100 customer-specific fine-tunes cheaply.
short: Train each as a LoRA on one shared base; serve the base once and load LoRA modules per request with batched multi-LoRA kernels; cache hot adapters on GPU; version and evaluate each.
